newsitem.title: CANADA: FREESTYLE SKIING-CANADA RULES WORLD CUP AERIALS.
newsitem.headline: FREESTYLE SKIING-CANADA RULES WORLD CUP AERIALS.

text.p: Canada ruled at the freestyle skiing World Cup aerials competition Sunday with a pair of 1-2 finishes at Blackcomb.
Caroline Olivier moved out of the shadow of her teammate Veronica Brenner with a two-jump score of 169 that gave her the gold ahead of Brenner, who has three World Cup wins this season.
Nicolas Fontaine, whose eight medals over the past three years have all been bronze, broke that string with a convincing victory in the men's final over Lloyd Langlois.
The Canadian sweep came in rain-saoked conditions that dealyed the event for more than an hour and concerned organisers that the event might not be completed by dark.
Olivier achieved her victory in spectacular fashion, following a reasonable first-round jump with a triple-twisting double somersault for the first time in competition.
"I finally did my new jump," said Olivier, posting her second World Cup victory after breaking through last season. "I think I was more surprised than anyone else."
Fontaine's win stopped his streak of eight straight World Cup bronze medals over the past three years. His last non-bronze was a gold at Blackcomb in 1994.
Notable absentees from the competition were injured Alexis Blanc of France and his teammate Sebastien Foucras.
